post_title: How many postal ballots will Correos report as admitted for Spain's 29 November 2026 general election in the most recent figure it publishes on or before 26 November 2026?

question.title: How many postal ballots will Correos report as admitted for Spain's 29 November 2026 general election in the most recent figure it publishes on or before 26 November 2026?
question.description:
Spain holds elections to the Cortes Generales on Sunday 29 November 2026. Postal voting is handled by the state postal operator Correos on behalf of the Oficina del Censo Electoral: voters resident in Spain could request a postal vote from 6 October until 19 November 2026, the provincial census delegations began mailing ballot papers and envelopes on 9 November, and completed ballots must be deposited at any Correos office by 25 November 2026 (https://www.correos.com/sala-prensa/asi-es-el-voto-por-correo-en-las-elecciones-generales-del-29-de-noviembre/ ; https://www.correos.es/es/es/particulares/para-el-ciudadano/voto-por-correo). Voters registered abroad (CERA) have a slightly different calendar, with consular deposit between 21 and 26 November and postal sending by 24 November.

Correos publishes cumulative press releases through each election cycle: first the number of postal-vote applications admitted, then - after the deposit deadline - the number of postal ballots actually admitted. For the 23 July 2023 general election it reported 2,622,808 applications admitted on 14 July 2023 (https://www.correos.com/sala-prensa/correos-ha-admitido-mas-de-26-millones-de-solicitudes-de-voto-por-correo-para-las-elecciones-generales-del-23-de-julio), then 2,461,284 ballots admitted as of the night of 20-21 July (the deposit deadline was 14:00 on 20 July) and a final 2,471,935 on 22 July - 94.2% of applications and the highest figures of the democratic era, 99.08% above the 1,241,716 ballots admitted in April 2019 (https://www.correos.com/sala-prensa/exito-en-la-gestion-del-voto-por-correo-que-marca-record-historico-con-2-471-935-votos-admitidos-para-las-elecciones-generales). For the 10 November 2019 election, the comparable release appeared on 8 November - the deposit-deadline day - reporting 900,188 ballots already sent (https://www.correos.com/sala-prensa/900-000-ciudadanos-ya-han-enviado-su-voto-por-correo-para-las-elecciones-a-cortes-generales-del-10-de-noviembre). Since 2008, between 6% and 9% of applicants have ended up not casting a postal ballot.

As of 13 November 2026, Correos has published no cumulative figure for the 29N election; its 10 November 2026 release only sets out the calendar. The historical pattern suggests a total-applications figure will appear shortly after the 19 November application deadline (a strong anchor available to forecasters when this question opens) and a cumulative ballots-admitted figure in the days immediately after the 25 November deposit deadline - the figure this question asks about. November elections have drawn far fewer postal votes than summer ones (roughly 0.9-1.0 million ballots admitted in November 2019 versus 2.47 million in July 2023), which, combined with this cycle's political salience, leaves the level genuinely uncertain.

Postal voting is politically contested in 2026: Vox leader Santiago Abascal has said he will not vouch for the "cleanliness" of postal voting and has urged voters not to use it, the government describes the system as "100% secure", and the PP has demanded additional guarantees and access to the daily reports Correos sends to the Interior Ministry.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the cumulative national number of postal ballots reported by Correos as admitted, deposited or sent ("votos admitidos", "votos emitidos", "votos depositados" or "enviados") for the 29 November 2026 Spanish general election, in the most recent Correos press release with a publication date of 26 November 2026 or earlier (Correos dates its releases in Madrid local time), as listed in its press room at https://www.correos.com/press-release-category/voto-por-correo/ . Counts of postal-vote applications ("solicitudes") are not used. Only the headline national cumulative total stated by Correos is used, exactly as published; no adjustment is made and regional or foreign-constituency (CERA) breakdowns are not summed. As an example of the metric, Correos' 22 July 2023 release (https://www.correos.com/sala-prensa/exito-en-la-gestion-del-voto-por-correo-que-marca-record-historico-con-2-471-935-votos-admitidos-para-las-elecciones-generales) reported 2,471,935 ballots admitted for the 23 July 2023 election, which would resolve as 2471935; if Correos states such a total only approximately (e.g. "more than 2.4 million"), the stated number is used (2,400,000). If no cumulative ballots-admitted figure for the 29N election has been published by that cutoff, the question is annulled.
question.fine_print: If Correos' press-room listing is unavailable or not yet updated, the figure published in the corresponding Correos press note (including its PDF version) or reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) citing Correos is used. Any extension of the ballot-deposit deadline by the Junta Electoral Central does not change the cutoff date.
